q: A grayscale image stored with 8 bits per pixel can show how many grey levels?
What does an image histogram count?
why: Each bar is the number of pixels with that grey level.

q: A histogram bunched to the left (dark side) usually means the image is…
why: Most pixels are dark, so the image is underexposed.
Each pixel becomes 0 or 1 depending on whether it is above the threshold.

q: Which method picks a threshold automatically from the histogram?
why: Otsu's method picks the threshold that best separates two classes of pixels.

q: Which filter is best at removing salt-and-pepper noise?
why: The median ignores the extreme black and white outliers.

q: A 3×3 averaging (mean) filter makes an image…
why: Averaging neighbours removes fine detail and noise: it is a low-pass filter.
It is a 3×3 projective map between two views of a plane, like the screen seen by the camera.

q: How many point pairs do you need, at least, to compute a homography?
why: Each pair gives 2 equations and a homography has 8 unknowns, so 4 pairs.

q: Morphological opening (erosion then dilation) is used to…
why: Erosion deletes small blobs; dilation restores the size of what survived.

q: VisionTouch finds your hand by subtracting which two images?
why: The engine predicts what the camera should see; whatever differs is in front of the screen.
